turns.speaker: facilitator
turns.text: You're building a copilot for live customer discovery calls. In one sentence, what does it have to do?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: As a discovery call happens, it has to listen to the conversation and derive candidate requirements in real time — objectives, needs, constraints, risks — and keep every single one traceable back to the exact words in the transcript that produced it.

turns.speaker: facilitator
turns.text: Traceable how, concretely? What has to be recorded for each derived item?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Every candidate artifact has to record its source evidence, an interpretation rationale, a confidence score, the derivation method, and a validation state. If I can't see why the tool proposed a requirement, I won't trust it.

turns.speaker: facilitator
turns.text: What's the rule about confirming a requirement the model only inferred?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: A model-inferred requirement must never be marked customer-confirmed without an explicit human action. Human validation before baselining is non-negotiable — that's the whole point of the tool.

turns.speaker: facilitator
turns.text: How does the transcript get in? Live microphone only?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Live microphone over a streaming connection is the main path, but we also need to upload a recorded file and run it through the exact same pipeline, so an upload yields the same segments and derived artifacts as the live call.

turns.speaker: facilitator
turns.text: Any constraint on the speech-to-text side?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Speech-to-text has to be provider-neutral — a mock, a local model, or a hosted vendor — and the provider credentials must stay server-side, never in the browser. And it has to run with no API keys at all by default, so anyone can try it.

turns.speaker: facilitator
turns.text: You mentioned a script earlier. Where does that fit?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: The facilitator follows a configurable discovery script, but a customer answer can spawn a conversation branch, and each branch has to keep its own evidence and derived artifacts. The scripted flow stays the anchor.

turns.speaker: facilitator
turns.text: And at the end of a session?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: At the end we export a structured discovery package as JSON and Markdown. That package is the deliverable — the requirements with their evidence, ready to hand to whoever architects the solution.

turns.speaker: facilitator
turns.text: Great — real-time evidence-traced derivation, human confirmation before baseline, provider-neutral speech-to-text, scripted flow plus branches, and a JSON and Markdown export. Let me play those back.
